hints.title: Score Sorted Index Pairing
hints.text: Athletes are ranked strictly by score in descending order. Pairing each score with its initial array index preserves placement mapping after sorting.

hints.title: Medal Substitution Invariant
hints.text: The top three indices receive Gold Medal, Silver Medal, and Bronze Medal respectively, while all remaining indices receive their rank number string.

hints.title: Descending Sort Rank Assignment Procedure
hints.text: Pair each score with its index and sort in descending order. Initialize a result array of size n. For ranks 0, 1, and 2, assign Gold Medal, Silver Medal, and Bronze Medal at original indices. For ranks three and above, assign string rank plus one. Return result array.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N log N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Repeatedly finding the maximum element takes quadratic O(N^2) time across large contestant rosters.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting index pairs takes O(N log N) time and requires O(N) space for index mappings and results.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should preserve original indices via pairing and handle the top three medal string substitutions cleanly.
